claims.statement: The Integration listing issue form captures structured listing metadata, labels submissions `integration-submission` and `integration`, and says a maintainer must apply `integration-run` to generate a docs PR.

The integration-submission workflow runs for a labeled issue or manual dispatch, but only proceeds for `integration-run` label events or dispatch; it uses a per-issue non-cancelling concurrency group.

Before checkout, the workflow authorizes the triggering actor through the repository collaborator permission API; only admin, maintain, and write are allowed, while an unauthorized issue-label event removes `integration-run`, comments, and skips.

The issue parser maps rendered form headings to stable fields without executing or evaluating values, normalizes optional empty responses, and rejects missing required fields and language-appropriate package names.
A successfully parsed issue is marked `integration-automation`; that label suppresses duplicate processing, and parse failure produces an issue comment without running the agent.

The trusted workflow explicitly treats form JSON as untrusted metadata, directs the agent to leave edits uncommitted and not perform GitHub mutations, and invokes Deep Agents with the `submit-integration` skill.
Hosted guides require at least 50,000 monthly PyPI or npm downloads or a maintainer featured decision; other integrations receive an external listing rather than a new hosted MDX page.

For external listings, `integration_external_docs.yaml` is the canonical language/component metadata source; the refresh script merges its rows with hosted-guide frontmatter, links external names to `docs_url`, and validates URLs to allow HTTP(S) or single-slash site-relative paths only.

Generated integration downloads snippets are written by `refresh_integration_downloads.py`; they must not be hand-edited, and the weekly update workflow regenerates them along with package and provider-overview artifacts before opening a PR only when changes exist.

The workflow reports blocker-file, failed-agent, and no-change outcomes on the issue instead of opening a PR; for real edits it creates an `integration/issue-<number>` PR with a review checklist, then links and mentions the PR on the source issue.
Retries after parse failure, agent failure, or no-change require removing `integration-automation` and having a maintainer reapply `integration-run`.

The refresh script retries npm and PyPI download fetches up to six times after HTTP 429 with exponential backoff, and the row resolver degrades other request or parsing failures to unavailable download data rather than failing table collection.
Focused unit tests cover parser extraction and the Python package requirement, plus external-URL safety, safe rendered links, repository-YAML URL validation, and table-text normalization.

`.agents/skills/` is the canonical project skill directory and has higher Deep Agents precedence than the former `.deepagents/skills/` location, so the workflow's `submit-integration` skill reference needs no symlink or shim.

The weekly refresh job flags external integrations at the 50,000-download threshold, creating deduplicated Linear issues only when both Linear credentials are configured and otherwise performing a dry run.

`packages.yml` is the source of truth for LangChain package and repository records and feeds the package index and partner package table; its `highlight` field is a maintainer-only download-filter override.
CI runs `refresh_integration_downloads.py --check-docs-urls` in a read-only job to validate external documentation URL schemes.

`packages_yml_get_downloads.py` rejects duplicate package names, skips records updated within 24 hours, records a missing Pepy badge as zero downloads, and writes refreshed download timestamps for fetched package records.

External entries with a missing `docs_url` are skipped during table collection, while an unsafe `docs_url` raises an error; the dedicated validation mode reports both missing and unsafe values before any writes.
The scheduled refresh passes only `packages.yml`, the Python provider overview, and generated integration snippets from its read-only generation job to the write-capable PR job.

The generated provider overview is produced by `partner_pkg_table.py` from `packages.yml`; CI regenerates it and fails when the checked-in generated file differs, directing changes to the generator or package metadata.

The integration table renderer selects component-specific chat, middleware, retriever, and conditionally populated vectorstore columns; it uses numeric download sort values for first paint and offline fallback while client-side code may refresh ordering later.

The hosted-docs candidate flagger accepts an optional threshold, uses component curation bars for issue context, and deduplicates Linear work by searching a stable title fragment that excludes changing download counts.

Candidate collection for hosted-docs Linear issues only requires a nonempty `docs_url`; it does not apply the renderer's URL-scheme validator, so candidate output is not a safe-link validation boundary.
An external row with no usable language-specific package is still collected and rendered with unavailable download data, whereas rows with no `docs_url` are excluded.
